content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text compares the challenger's and defender's chains by footing in a chain-versus-chain collision, so K-C governs.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter; the defender's chain is footed but rests on the woman-route inference.", "rule_words": "A link is judged by its support, never by whether any verse, or the chain as a whole, states it word for word; and a verse whose words leave the question open decides nothing by itself. When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.", "room": "never verse by verse — read as barring reliance on a chain's failure to explicitly name the proposition, versus read as only barring tallying individual verses while allowing explicit-naming findings.", "why": "The judge penalizes a footed chain for not explicitly naming Joseph and another footed chain for resting on inference, so it weighs by explicit wording rather than by chain footing."}
